# [BUG] ai-service missing ACTOR_SERVICE_BASE_URL override in aws/azure/local k8s overlays

## Bug
`infrastructure/kubernetes/overlays/{aws,azure,local}/kustomization.yaml`
each disable Eureka for ai-service (`EUREKA_CLIENT_ENABLED=false`) and
override `MOVIE_SERVICE_BASE_URL=http://movie-service:8081` to bypass
`lb://` load-balancer resolution — but none of the three set an
equivalent `ACTOR_SERVICE_BASE_URL`, a config key #203
(`ActorCatalogClient`/`RestClientConfig`) just introduced.

With Eureka disabled and no override, `ActorCatalogClient`'s `RestClient`
stays at its `lb://actor-service` default, which
`BlockingLoadBalancerInterceptor` cannot resolve without Eureka. Every
call `ActorCatalogClient` makes fails at request time in these three
deployment targets — not a crash (the client degrades gracefully to an
empty result, per its own design), but every natural-language search
with a named person (#198/#203's whole point) silently returns zero
results, with nothing surfaced beyond a `WARN` log line.

Confirmed live only in the sense of reading the actual kustomization
files (grep — no `ACTOR_SERVICE_BASE_URL` reference anywhere in the
repo); not yet reproduced against a running `aws`/`azure`/`local`
deployment.

## Root Cause
Missing `ACTOR_SERVICE_BASE_URL=http://actor-service:8083` (matching the
existing `MOVIE_SERVICE_BASE_URL` pattern and actor-service's own port,
per `docker-compose.yml`/the base manifest) in each of the three
overlays' `ai-service-config` `configMapGenerator` block.

## Severity vs. Priority
**Severity (technical impact):** Major — a real feature (#198's whole
Story) silently non-functional in 3 of 4 deployment targets, degrading
rather than crashing so it's easy to miss without dedicated testing.
**Priority (business urgency):** P2 — not urgent (the Story's frontend
tasks, #204-206, aren't done yet either, so nothing user-facing is live
against these overlays today), but should land before #204/#205 make
this reachable from the UI in a deployed environment.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `ACTOR_SERVICE_BASE_URL` added to all three overlays'
      `ai-service-config` block, mirroring `MOVIE_SERVICE_BASE_URL`
- [ ] Verified live against at least one of the three overlays (or the
      closest feasible local equivalent) — a natural-language search
      involving a named person actually reaches actor-service, not just
      a config-file diff
- [ ] Regression note: worth a brief check whenever a new ai-service
      downstream client is added, so this doesn't recur for a future
      service

## Notes
Surfaced during #203's independent code review, not by a live incident —
flagged rather than fixed in that Task's own diff to keep its scope to
"aggregation logic" per its own Scope note, and because editing
deployment manifests bundled into a feature commit is worth a human's
eyes rather than silent inclusion.
